subject: System Design
title: YouTube's Video Processing
description: A micro-lesson that makes YouTube's Video Processing usable.

hook.text: 500 hours of video are uploaded to YouTube every minute. Processing that volume is a scale problem few companies face.

buildup.text: Each upload is transcoded into dozens of formats: 144p to 8K, VP9 and AV1 codecs, HDR and SDR versions.

discovery.text: YouTube uses a massive distributed pipeline. Transcoding jobs are parallelized across thousands of machines.

twist.text: Processing isn't instant. Popular videos get priority. A viral video may be transcoded to 4K faster than a cat video.

climax.text: YouTube's pipeline handles more video in one day than all TV networks produced in decades — fully automated.

punchline.text: Upload once, transcode to dozens of formats in parallel.

quiz.question: Why does YouTube transcode videos into multiple formats?
options: Different devices and connections need different resolutions and codecs
